_about: The blind proof of the story engine v5 (scripts/post-pack/story_proof.py; docs/plans/proofs/2026-11-26-story-engine-v5/PROTOCOL.md). The evaluator, never a scorer: it may read his picks to pair cards, and story_score.py never imports it. The thresholds live in PROTOCOL.md, frozen before any paid call; this file holds the harness's wording and limits only.

card._about: One renderer for both sides of a pair (story_proof.card): the slot, what happened (the sourced fact) and the angle, each cut to its word limit, and the source's site only. strip_patterns are taken out first (a leading 'Publication, date:' prefix, since the source line names the site; board notes on what a card was rebuilt from), then a sentence that talks about the board is dropped, then the house labels. With no engine angle, the option's own angle stands, else its title.

pool_draft._about: A gather-pool story as a draft option for Arm S: the scorer reads these fields only (story_score blind_view keeps them). The title is the idea's first sentence. Each hero day keeps its board options and adds its series pool's best shortlist_per_day stories by fit plus named_thing (the Sunday procedure's deterministic shortlist, no call); the stories with no series (unassigned), best first, fill each day's places left, Monday, Wednesday, Friday in turn. So the paid steps read a bounded pool.

sheet.title: Story engine blind proof
sheet.intro: Each pair is two stories for the same slot of a past week. Which would you rather make and read? Answer each pair on its line: A++ or B++ for a clear win, A+ or B+ for a lean, = for no difference. Say whether you have seen either before, and whether you would make each. Notes are optional. Nothing here is on the board.
sheet.tells_intro: Each pair below is two stories for the same slot. One was chosen by a new story engine and one was on the old board. For each pair say which card you think the new engine chose, as `Pnn: A` or `Pnn: B`, with one short reason. Judge only what is on the cards.
